record.title: A study finds BF16 and FP16 can produce different greedy LLM outputs
record.summary: A September 2026 TMLR paper reports that BF16 versus FP16 inference produced different greedy-decoding sequences on 49–100% of prompts across six tested models and three benchmarks. The authors report that recomputing only the language-model output head in FP32 when the top-two logit margin is small improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on an A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 GPUs, with under 4% latency overhead at batch sizes up to 4. They report that the intervention’s benefit disappears at batch size 8 or higher and under end-to-end FP8. These are author-reported results, not an independent reproduction.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The TMLR paper was published in September 2026 and is available through its arXiv record and PDF.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report BF16/FP16 greedy-decoding sequences diverged on 49–100% of prompts across six 1.1B–7B models, four model families and three benchmarks; a separate 12.2B test characterized divergence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that selective FP32 LM-head recomputation at low top-two margins improved exact sequence agreement by 22–36 percentage points on A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 with less than 4% latency overhead at batch size <=4.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that the intervention’s benefit vanishes at batch size >=8 and under end-to-end FP8; it is not a universal determinism guarantee.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the cross-precision divergence rates or selective LM-head intervention was performed.
The paper does not establish how often this issue occurs in production serving configurations or on larger/closed models.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported cross-precision divergence and gated repair generalize, they affect reproducibility and evaluation in model serving across common deployment formats. The paper reports multi-model results, but the bounded experiments and unverified external reproduction make this a notable engineering concern rather than a universal determinism failure.
limitations: All numerical performance findings are the paper authors’ reports and were not independently reproduced.
Divergence and repair effectiveness vary by model, GPU, batch size and precision regime; the intervention is not universal.
The low-overhead repair applies only to low-batch single-stream settings in the paper; benefit disappears at batch size >=8 and under tested end-to-end FP8.

The paper studies selected 1.1B–7B models and benchmarks, with a separate 12.2B divergence characterization; it does not establish prevalence for closed models, production workloads or all numerical formats.
brief.summary: A September 2026 TMLR paper reports that BF16 versus FP16 inference produced different greedy-decoding sequences on 49–100% of prompts across six tested models and three benchmarks. The authors report that recomputing only the language-model output head in FP32 when the top-two logit margin is small improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on an A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 GPUs, with under 4% latency overhead at batch sizes up to 4. They report that the intervention’s benefit disappears at batch size 8 or higher and under end-to-end FP8. These are author-reported results, not an independent reproduction.

technical.claimed_result: The paper reports 49–100% prompt-level BF16/FP16 sequence divergence across six 1.1B–7B models, four model families and three benchmarks; a separate 12.2B test characterizes divergence. Selective FP32 LM-head recomputation reportedly raises exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 with less than 4% latency overhead for batch size <=4.
technical.compute_or_cost: Authors report <4% latency overhead for selective recomputation in the stated low-batch regime.
technical.demonstrated_result: The publication event and paper contents were inspected. Numerical performance values below are author-reported and are not independently demonstrated in this review.
technical.implementation_status: The paper describes and evaluates an inference-time intervention; this review did not run the code or verify deployment in a serving stack.
technical.mechanism: The authors attribute cross-format token flips to small top-two logit margins when BF16/FP16 rounding perturbs the output-head decision. Their selective intervention recomputes the LM head in FP32 only when the margin falls below a threshold.
technical.novelty: The paper combines output-level cross-precision measurements, controlled mechanism analysis and a margin-triggered output-head recomputation; the authors distinguish this from known within-format nondeterminism.
technical.regime: Paper experiments compare BF16 and FP16 on the same hardware for autoregressive greedy decoding, mainly on small open-weight models and selected benchmarks. The gated intervention is reported for low-batch single-stream inference (batch <=4); gains vanish at batch >=8 and under end-to-end FP8.
technical.reproducibility: Paper reports experiments; independent reproduction and production-serving verification remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares the intervention against unmodified inference and broader-scope FP32 recomputation. The authors report broader FP32 scope can reduce agreement; no external reproduction was located.

brief.title: A study finds BF16 and FP16 can produce different greedy LLM outputs
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported regime-specific effect generalizes, serving precision can change exact model behavior even under greedy decoding, complicating cross-system replay and evaluation. The paper also offers a targeted but explicitly partial mitigation; its bounded workload and batch limits determine where the result applies.
